_README: Experiment configuration for the terrain-blind predictive ML layer.
Every value here is either a decision recorded with its reason, or a
number DERIVED FROM DATA with the derivation named. Nothing is a guess.
Consumed by the planner, the forecaster evaluation, and the PPO reward;
the simulator reads its own constants from scripts/auto_patrol.py.
Regenerate the derived values with: python3 scripts/derive_thresholds.py

_rsrp_floor_provenance: DERIVED 2026-10-19 from 5854 pooled (RSRP, C2) observations across all
five archive terrains. The brief's default of -80 dBm is unusable: the
minimum RSRP ever observed is -78 dBm and ZERO rows fall below -80, so
margin = rsrp - floor is identically positive and the soft-min objective
in brief 5.3 has nothing to optimise.
C2 availability has a clear knee: <-75 dBm 13.0%, -75..-70 28.9%,
At -68 dBm: 34.5% availability below vs 93.8% above (59 pp gap) with
5.6% of rows below — both discriminative and non-degenerate.
CAVEAT 1: derived from the INTEGER dBm field, which is a 1 dB
truncation. ss_rsrp_dBre now logs full precision; re-derive from new
campaign data, the floor may shift ~1 dB.
CAVEAT 2: indoor does NOT separate at this floor (8.3% vs 18.2%)
because everything there was failing. Recheck after the geometry retune.
_sinr_floor_provenance: DERIVED by the same procedure as the RSRP floor: 31.4% availability
below vs 93.7% above (62.3 pp gap) with 5.1% of rows below.
Marginally the stronger discriminator of the two, but the brief

_c2_rule_note: Brief 5.2. Ping loss is close to the label, so every forecaster result
must be reported WITH and WITHOUT ping-loss history as an input.

_note: The fast horizons need the 10 Hz fast-radio log (scripts/
fast_radio_sampler.py). The per-cycle CSV cannot support them: its
median cadence is 22.8 s with 2 robots and roughly double with 4,
so a 30 s history window spans ~1.3 rows (DATA_AUDIT.md 4.1).

_dwell_note: Long dwell keeps each slow measurement cycle inside one action, which
the per-cycle throughput and C2 columns need to be attributable.
Short dwell roughly triples labelled actions per hour for the
surrogate, which trains off the 10 Hz log where action boundaries are
exact regardless of dwell. Campaign seed round 0 uses long, later

_indoor_note: Indoor was coverage-dead until 2026-10-19: a +-35 m UAV wander box
around a 60x40 m building parked the node 30-35 m away at 15-35 m
altitude. The O2I model was never the limiter — it matches 3GPP
TR 38.901 and contributes only 11.5-14 dB. Geometry retuned to a
+-32 m box at 8-20 m so the node can circle the perimeter closely.
This CHANGES THE SCENARIO rather than fixing a bug, and belongs in
the paper's method section: the old setup was not wrong, it was
hopeless, and a scenario where no action helps teaches nothing.
_robot_note: the published 2-robot SATNAC configuration exactly. 4-robot data is
NOT directly comparable to the 2-robot baseline — four UEs share one
gNB, so scheduling contention differs. Treat them as separate

splits._note: Brief 7. Random row splits leak across the history window.

_provenance: MEASURED 2026-10-20 with a dependency-free TCP harness, 30 s
sustained uplink, every figure confirmed at the receiver.
1 robot 18.5 Mb/s; 4 robots ~17.7 Mb/s aggregate (~4.4 each).
The cell tops out near 18 Mb/s TOTAL and shares it evenly.
NOT a 5G configuration limit: during a healthy flow the gNB runs
MCS 28 / Qm 6 (64QAM) / NPRB 106 at 23-25 dB SNR with BLER 0.
The binding constraint is the rfsimulator RU thread at 93% of one
core while the box sits near 31%. No config change moves it.
Traffic is UPLINK: the iperf3 client runs inside the robot netns,
so robots are senders. See DATA_AUDIT.md section 10.

_calibration: CALIBRATED 2026-10-21 by running the real excitation policy at three
rates, each with fresh iperf3 servers and the 10-packet C2 ping:
Too low: throughput pinned at the cap, carries no link information.
Too high: cell saturates as the UAV roams, C2 collapses to 41%
(7-11% at long range) and the keep-connected objective is saturated
at DISCONNECTED with no headroom for the planner to improve.
2.5 keeps both alive: C2 grades 95/79/59/41% across distance bands.

iperf3_abi_clash: different ABI -> 'stack smashing detected' and SIGSEGV. Flows died
mid-test and were relaunched; that, NOT UE reattach, caused the
throughput restart artifacts. 3.16 backed up to
and gazebo_viz.py (3.9 predates it, and it is redundant inside the
robot netns where the UE tun is the only route to the test IP).

_note: FIXED 2026-10-21. Was `ping -c 2`, so loss could only be 0/50/100%
and the label 'loss < 50%' required BOTH packets to arrive. That
biases hard toward failure: 90% per-packet delivery reads as 81%,
70% reads as 49%. Switching to 10 packets raised measured
availability from 28% to 47% on identical traffic.
